question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to replace the word in brackets.
The author's writing was so captivating that readers were [enthralled], while the other book left them completely uninterested.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. bored.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Enthralled" means captivated, fascinated, or held spellbound by something extremely interesting or delightful. (मंत्रमुग्ध/मोहित)
◦ Example: The children were enthralled by the magician's tricks.

• Its most appropriate antonym is "Bored", meaning feeling weary and uninterested because of a lack of engagement. (ऊबा हुआ/अरुचि रखने वाला) The sentence itself confirms this, contrasting readers who were enthralled with those left "completely uninterested" by the other book.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Interested" (रुचि रखने वाला): This is closer to a synonym of "enthralled" rather than its opposite, since an enthralled reader is, by definition, highly interested.

• Option 2: "Agreement" (सहमति): This word relates to consent or accord and has no direct connection to the emotional state of being captivated or bored; it does not fit as an antonym.

• Option 4: "Intrigued" (उत्सुक/जिज्ञासु): This means having one's curiosity aroused, which is a synonym of "enthralled", not its antonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "enthralled": captivated, spellbound, mesmerized, fascinated, riveted.

• Other antonyms of "enthralled": indifferent, apathetic, uninterested, weary.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.
This library building is very high and has 25 floors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Low.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "High" means elevated, tall, or extending a great distance upward. (ऊँचा)
◦ Example: The high tower could be seen from miles away.

• Its most appropriate antonym is "Low", meaning not high; close to the ground or of small height. (नीचा/निम्न)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Sturdy" (मजबूत): Means strongly built or firm; it relates to strength, not to height, so it cannot be the antonym of "high".

• Option 3: "Hale" (स्वस्थ/तंदुरुस्त): Means healthy and robust, typically used for a person's physical condition; it is unrelated to the concept of height.

• Option 4: "Elevated" (ऊँचा उठा हुआ): This is a synonym of "high", not its antonym, since it also means raised or lifted to a higher position.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "high": tall, lofty, towering, elevated.

• Other antonyms of "high": short, low-lying, stunted, squat.

question:
In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement.
O: that the Soviet army had liberated
P: from the fascist forces came under
Q: the east European countries
R: the control of the USSR
S: after the Second World War
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. SQOPR.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To solve a parajumble, first identify the segment that can logically begin the sentence and then trace the chain of ideas that follows it in a grammatically and logically coherent manner.

• Segment S ("after the Second World War") is a time-phrase that naturally opens the sentence, since it sets the historical context for what follows.

• Segment Q ("the east European countries") must follow S, as it introduces the subject of the sentence.

• Segment O ("that the Soviet army had liberated") is a relative clause that must immediately follow Q, since it describes/modifies "the east European countries".

• Segments P ("from the fascist forces came under") and R ("the control of the USSR") complete the verb phrase, explaining what the countries came under, after being freed "from the fascist forces".

• Combining all segments: "After the Second World War, the east European countries that the Soviet army had liberated from the fascist forces came under the control of the USSR." This gives the order S-Q-O-P-R.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: SROPQ is incorrect because placing R ("the control of the USSR") directly after S breaks the logical subject-verb chain and produces a meaningless sequence.

• Option 2: POQSR is incorrect because it begins with P ("from the fascist forces came under"), which cannot start the sentence as it lacks a subject.

• Option 3: POSQR is incorrect for the same reason — starting with P leaves the sentence without an opening subject, and the subsequent order of O, S, Q, R does not form a coherent statement.

NOTE

• In parajumbles, always look for: (i) the segment introducing the subject/topic, (ii) linking words or pronouns (such as "that", "which", "it") that connect to an earlier segment, and (iii) time markers (such as "after", "before") that often work well as sentence openers.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Ranveer never has the habit of making a beeline for his academic activities.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. going straight and quick.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To make a beeline (for something)" means to go straight and quickly towards something/somewhere, without any delay or detour. (सीधे और तेज़ी से किसी ओर जाना)
◦ Example: As soon as the bell rang, the children made a beeline for the canteen.

• The idiom is derived from the straight-line flight path a bee takes back to its hive.

• Applying this meaning to the sentence: Ranveer never goes straight and quickly (i.e., is never prompt/direct) about his academic activities.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Behaving abnormally": This refers to unusual conduct and has no connection with speed or directness of movement, so it does not match the idiom's meaning.

• Option 2: "Selecting inconsiderately": This implies making careless choices, which is unrelated to the idea of moving swiftly and directly towards something.

• Option 4: "Immediately responding to things": This relates to a quick reaction or reply, not to physically or figuratively heading straight towards a goal, so it does not fully capture the idiom's sense of direct movement.

NOTE

• Other idioms of speed/promptness often asked in SSC: "At the drop of a hat" (immediately, without hesitation), "In a jiffy" (very quickly), "Post-haste" (with great speed).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Rohit did not slap Kunal.
option_1: Kunal was not being slapped by Rohit.
option_2: Kunal had not been slapped by Rohit.
option_3: Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.
option_4: Kunal has not been slapped by Rohit.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Rohit did not slap Kunal" is a negative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + did not + V1 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + not + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "Kunal" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary used is "was"; the base verb "slap" becomes the past participle "slapped"; and "Rohit" becomes the agent introduced with "by".
◦ Passive: Kunal was not slapped by Rohit.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "was not being slapped" is the passive form of the Past Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had not been slapped" is the passive form of the Past Perfect Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has not been slapped" is the passive form of the Present Perfect Tense, which does not match the tense of the original sentence.

NOTE

• In the passive voice, the tense of the auxiliary verb must always match the tense of the active sentence; only the subject-object positions and the main verb form (into V3) change.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.
The company understood that these small protests of employees regarding low wages were just the tip of the iceberg.
option_1: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is non-existent
option_2: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is solvable
option_3: A large part of a problem which is really noticeable
option_4: A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. A small, noticeable part of a problem, the total size of which is really much greater.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "The tip of the iceberg" means a small, visible part of a much larger problem or situation, most of which remains hidden. (समस्या का एक छोटा-सा दिखने वाला हिस्सा, जबकि असली समस्या कहीं बड़ी है)
◦ Example: The reported cases of fraud are just the tip of the iceberg; the actual scale of corruption is far larger.

• The expression comes from the fact that only about one-tenth of an iceberg is visible above the water's surface, while the much larger mass remains submerged and unseen.

• Applying this to the sentence: the small protests were only a visible sign of a much bigger, underlying problem regarding low wages.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: States that "the total size of which is non-existent," which is the opposite of the idiom's actual meaning — the hidden part is very much real and large, not non-existent.

• Option 2: States that the total size "is solvable," but the idiom makes no claim about whether the larger problem can be solved; it only emphasises that the visible part is small compared to the whole.

• Option 3: Incorrectly describes the visible part itself as "large," whereas the idiom specifically refers to a small, noticeable part representing a much larger hidden whole.

NOTE

• Other idioms describing scale/magnitude often asked in SSC: "A drop in the ocean" (a very small amount compared to what is needed), "The straw that broke the camel's back" (the final small factor that causes a collapse after a long strain).

question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence.
A. The world's biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico.
B. It is called Arecibo dish.
C. It was built 40 years ago.
D. It is also 300 metres across.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. ABDC.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sentence A introduces the main topic — "The world's biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico" — and therefore must be the opening sentence, as every other sentence uses the pronoun "It" to refer back to this telescope.

• Sentence B logically follows A, giving the telescope's name: "It is called Arecibo dish."

• Sentence D continues describing the telescope's physical features after it has been named: "It is also 300 metres across." The word "also" signals that another descriptive fact (in addition to its name) is being added.

• Sentence C — "It was built 40 years ago" — comes last, as it shifts from describing the telescope's physical features to its history/age, forming a natural concluding fact.

• Combining all sentences in this order gives a coherent paragraph: "The world's biggest radio telescope is in Puerto Rico. It is called Arecibo dish. It is also 300 metres across. It was built 40 years ago." This gives the order A-B-D-C.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: CBDA is incorrect because it begins with C, which refers to "it" without first establishing what "it" is — the telescope must be introduced (as in A) before any pronoun can refer back to it.

• Option 3: DCAB is incorrect for the same reason — it opens with D, using "It" before the subject has been introduced by sentence A.

• Option 4: DCBA is incorrect because it places A, the essential introductory sentence, at the very end, which is illogical since all preceding sentences depend on it for context.

NOTE

• In sentence-ordering questions, always identify the sentence that introduces the main subject by name (rather than referring to it with a pronoun like "it/he/she/they") — that sentence must come first, and all pronoun-led sentences must follow it in a logically connected sequence.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who looks at the bright side of things/situations
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Optimist.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "Optimist" is one who looks at the bright side of things/situations and expects favourable outcomes. (आशावादी व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: Despite the setback, she remained an optimist, confident that things would improve.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Saint" (संत): A person recognised as holy or virtuous, especially in religious contexts; it has no connection with a hopeful outlook on situations.

• Option 3: "Pessimist" (निराशावादी): This is the exact opposite of the required word — one who expects the worst or focuses on the negative side of things.

• Option 4: "Scientist" (वैज्ञानिक): A person engaged in the systematic study of the natural world; it is unrelated to one's outlook on life.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often asked in SSC: "Pessimist" (one who looks at the dark/negative side of things), "Cynic" (one who believes people are motivated purely by self-interest), "Philanthropist" (one who works for the welfare of others).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Recieve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Receive" — to take, get, or be given something. The word given in Option 1, "Recieve", is incorrectly spelt.
◦ Example: She was delighted to receive the award for her outstanding performance.

• Spelling key: the word follows the rule "i before e, except after c" — since the "e" comes right after "c", the correct order is c-e-i, not c-i-e. So it is spelt R-E-C-E-I-V-E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Necessary" is correctly spelt — meaning something that is essential or required.

• Option 3: "Possession" is correctly spelt — meaning the state of owning or having something.

• Option 4: "Accommodate" is correctly spelt — meaning to provide lodging/space for someone, or to adapt to something. It is commonly misspelt because it has a double "c" and a double "m".

NOTE

• The "i before e, except after c" rule also applies to words like believe, achieve, field, ceiling, deceive, perceive. Exceptions to remember: weird, seize, either, neither, foreign, science.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Will you give me an independent project?
option_1: Will you be given an independent project by me?
option_2: Would an independent project be given?
option_3: Would I be given an independent project?
option_4: Will I be given an independent project by you?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Will I be given an independent project by you?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Will you give me an independent project?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Future Tense, beginning with the auxiliary/modal "Will".

• Rule — Passive of interrogative sentences with modal "Will" (Simple Future):
◦ Active: Will + Subject + V1 + Indirect Object + Direct Object?
◦ Passive: Will + (new subject, i.e. former indirect object) + be + V3 + by + (former subject)?

• Applying the rule: the indirect object "me" becomes the subject "I"; the modal "will" stays at the beginning, followed by "be"; the verb "give" becomes the past participle "given"; the direct object "an independent project" remains as it is; and the subject "you" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: Will I be given an independent project by you?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it wrongly makes "an independent project" the passive subject while retaining "me" as an object phrase, producing an ungrammatical and meaning-altered sentence: "Will you be given an independent project by me?" reverses who is giving and who is receiving.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it drops the agent "by you" and omits the new subject "I" altogether, making the sentence incomplete and unclear about who is asking.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it changes the modal from a question ("Will...?") to "Would...?", altering the tense/mood of the original sentence, and also omits the necessary agent "by you".

NOTE

• When converting an interrogative sentence beginning with a modal (Will/Can/May/Should, etc.) into the passive voice, the modal stays in its original position at the start of the sentence, followed by the new subject, then "be + V3".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The chair I have bought recently is costly than what I bought last year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. is costlier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence uses "is costly than", but the word "than" is a comparative conjunction that must always be preceded by a comparative degree adjective, never the positive degree ("costly").

• Rule — Comparative Degree: When two things are compared using "than", the adjective must be in the comparative form, usually formed by adding "-er" to short adjectives (or using "more" with longer ones).
◦ Example: Costly → Costlier than; Big → Bigger than; Beautiful → More beautiful than.

• Applying the rule: "costly" must be changed to its comparative form "costlier", giving: "The chair I have bought recently is costlier than what I bought last year."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is the costliest" uses the superlative degree, which is used to compare more than two items, not to compare with "than"; the superlative degree is also never followed by "than".

• Option 3: "was costly" incorrectly changes the tense to past, whereas the sentence describes a chair bought "recently" and refers to the present state, so the tense should remain in the present ("is").

• Option 4: "will be costly" incorrectly changes the tense to future, and also fails to provide the comparative form required before "than".

NOTE

• Words ending in a consonant + "y" form their comparative by changing "y" to "i" and adding "-er": e.g., happy → happier, easy → easier, costly → costlier.

• The comparative degree is always followed by "than", never by "from" or "to".

question:
Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank.
Akshaya ________________ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. studied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence contains two actions joined by "and": "Akshaya ___ hard for the entrance exam and received a high score." Since the second verb, "received", is in the Simple Past Tense, the first verb must also be in the Simple Past Tense to maintain parallel structure.

• Rule — Parallelism of tense: When two verbs are joined by a coordinating conjunction (and/but/or) and describe actions completed at the same time in the past, both verbs must be in the same tense.

• Applying the rule: the blank must be filled with the simple past form of "study", which is "studied".
◦ Complete sentence: "Akshaya studied hard for the entrance exam and received a high score."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "studies" is in the Simple Present Tense, which does not match the past tense verb "received" used later in the sentence.

• Option 2: "has studied" is in the Present Perfect Tense, which is inconsistent with the simple past tense of "received".

• Option 3: "was studied" is a passive construction ("was + V3"), which is grammatically incorrect here since Akshaya is the doer of the action (active voice is required, not passive).

NOTE

• When two verbs describing sequential or simultaneous past actions are joined by "and", both should generally be in the same tense (usually Simple Past) to maintain grammatical parallelism.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
His parents didn't allow him to enrol in the arts college because he is a dabbler in arts, science or literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dilettante.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Dilettante" is a person who dabbles/engages in arts, science, or literature merely as a pastime, without serious commitment or expertise. (कलाओं आदि का शौकिया अभ्यासी, जिसे गहरा ज्ञान न हो)
◦ Example: He was more of a dilettante than a serious painter, dabbling in art only on weekends.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Connoisseur" (पारखी): A person with expert knowledge and refined taste, especially in the fine arts, food, or wine — the opposite of a superficial dabbler.

• Option 2: "Taciturn" (मितभाषी/कम बोलने वाला): An adjective describing a person who says very little; it has no connection with arts or hobbies.

• Option 4: "Ignoramus" (अज्ञानी व्यक्ति): A person who is ignorant or lacks knowledge altogether, which is different from someone who dabbles superficially in a subject.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often asked in SSC: "Connoisseur" (an expert judge in matters of art/taste), "Amateur" (one who engages in a pursuit as a hobby, not professionally), "Virtuoso" (a person highly skilled in an art, especially music).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
He was the most honest and good-hearted man that she had ever met.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Sincere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "Honest" means truthful, fair, and free from deceit or fraud. (ईमानदार/सच्चा)
◦ Example: He gave an honest account of what had happened at the meeting.

• Its most appropriate synonym is "Sincere", meaning genuine, truthful, and free from pretence or deceit. (सच्चा/निष्कपट)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Deceptive" (धोखा देने वाला): Means misleading or intended to deceive, which is the opposite of "honest".

• Option 3: "Biased" (पक्षपाती): Means having an unfair preference or prejudice, which is unrelated to truthfulness and is not a synonym of "honest".

• Option 4: "Fake" (नकली/झूठा): Means not genuine or counterfeit, which is the opposite meaning of "honest".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "honest": truthful, upright, forthright, candid, genuine.

• Other antonyms of "honest": dishonest, deceitful, fraudulent, corrupt.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence.
I do not have any access to the information in this matter.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Denial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "Access" means the means or opportunity to approach, enter, or make use of something. (पहुँच/प्रवेश)
◦ Example: Employees have access to the company's confidential records.

• Its most appropriate antonym is "Denial", meaning the refusal of a request, or the act of being deprived of something. (इनकार/अस्वीकृति) In the sentence, not having "access" to information means one is effectively facing a "denial" of it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Doubt" (संदेह): Means a feeling of uncertainty; it does not relate to the idea of being granted or refused entry/use of something.

• Option 2: "Reach" (पहुँच): This is actually a synonym of "access" (both mean the ability to get to or contact something), not its antonym.

• Option 3: "Clue" (सुराग): Means a piece of evidence or information that helps solve a problem; it is unrelated to the concept of access.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "access": entry, admittance, approach, entrée.

• Other antonyms of "access": refusal, exclusion, denial, prohibition.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.
The teacher asked him not to keep disturbing the class, but it had no affect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. but it had no affect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of the word "affect". Here, a noun is required (meaning "a result or consequence"), and the correct noun for this meaning is "effect", not "affect".

• Rule — Affect vs Effect:
◦ "Affect" is normally used as a verb, meaning to influence something. Example: Smoking affects health.
◦ "Effect" is normally used as a noun, meaning a result or outcome. Example: The medicine had a positive effect.

• Applying the rule: since the sentence needs a noun after "no" ("had no ___"), the correct word is "effect", not "affect". The correct sentence should read: "...but it had no effect."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "him not to keep" is grammatically correct — "asked him not to keep doing something" is a standard structure.

• Option 3: "disturbing the class," is grammatically correct, correctly using the gerund form after "keep".

• Option 4: "The teacher asked" is grammatically correct as the opening subject-verb phrase of the sentence.

NOTE

• "Effect" can also be used as a verb meaning "to bring about" (e.g., to effect a change), and "affect" can rarely be used as a noun in psychology (meaning emotion/mood) — but for SSC exams, remember the standard usage: affect = verb (to influence), effect = noun (a result).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Profuse
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Scarce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Profuse" means abundant, plentiful, or given/occurring in generous or excessive amounts. (प्रचुर/अत्यधिक)
◦ Example: He offered profuse apologies for the delay.

• Its most appropriate antonym is "Scarce", meaning insufficient in quantity, or hard to find. (दुर्लभ/कमी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Humble" (विनम्र): Means modest or having a low estimate of one's own importance; it is unrelated to quantity or abundance.

• Option 3: "Prompt" (तुरंत/समयनिष्ठ): Means quick or done without delay; it does not relate to the idea of abundance or scarcity.

• Option 4: "Just" (न्यायसंगत): Means fair or reasonable; it has no connection with the meaning of quantity expressed by "profuse".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "profuse": abundant, copious, plentiful, lavish, ample.

• Other antonyms of "profuse": meagre, sparse, insufficient, limited.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
Even when he was left with plenty of fortune, he lived a frugal life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Thrifty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "Frugal" means careful and economical in the use of money or resources; avoiding waste. (मितव्ययी/कम खर्च करने वाला)
◦ Example: Despite being wealthy, she led a frugal life, avoiding unnecessary expenses.

• Its most appropriate synonym is "Thrifty", meaning careful with money and resources; not wasteful. (मितव्ययी)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Purposeless" (उद्देश्यहीन): Means lacking a purpose or aim, which has no relation to the idea of being economical.

• Option 3: "Extraordinary" (असाधारण): Means very unusual or remarkable, which is unrelated to the meaning of "frugal".

• Option 4: "Hardworking" (मेहनती): Means diligent or industrious, which describes effort, not economical use of money — unrelated to "frugal".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "frugal": economical, sparing, prudent, thrifty.

• Other antonyms of "frugal": extravagant, wasteful, lavish, prodigal.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
RN Right's literary works helped redefine discussions in race relations in America in the mid-20th century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. of race relations in America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun "discussions" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "of" (or "about") when specifying the topic being discussed, i.e., "discussions of/about [topic]".

• Rule — Preposition with "discussion(s)": When "discussion" refers to the subject matter under consideration, it takes the preposition "of" or "about", not "in", "by", "to", or "beside".
◦ Example: The book sparked fresh discussions of climate policy.

• Applying the rule: the correct phrase is "discussions of race relations in America", meaning discussions about/concerning race relations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "by race relations in America" is incorrect because "by" indicates an agent/means, which does not fit with specifying the topic of a discussion.

• Option 2: "beside race relations in America" is incorrect because "beside" means "next to" or "in comparison with", which does not make sense here.

• Option 3: "to race relations in America" is incorrect because "to" does not idiomatically follow "discussions" when introducing the topic being discussed.

NOTE

• Similar noun + preposition collocations often tested in SSC: "knowledge of", "interest in", "discussion of/about", "opinion about/on".

question: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
option_1: Researchers recommend that pesticides should not be used indiscriminately as they eliminate biodiversity for future generations.
option_2: Journalism is often the work of painstaking rigour and perseverence that detail the socio-political experiences of our worlds.
option_3: The venerated singer was also secretive, moody and very intense, famous for erratic and difficult behaviour
option_4: Elephants are in trouble mainly because people desire ivory trinkets that are made of tusks, often gruesomely killing them to achieve their purpose.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Journalism is often the work of painstaking rigour and perseverence that detail the socio-political experiences of our worlds.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Perseverence" used in this sentence is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Perseverance" — meaning persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success.
◦ Example: Her perseverance through years of hardship finally paid off.

• Spelling key: the word ends in "-ance", not "-ence" — remember it as PERSEVER + ANCE, derived from the verb "persevere".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correctly spelt throughout — "indiscriminately" and "biodiversity" are both spelt correctly.

• Option 3 is correctly spelt throughout — "venerated", "secretive", and "erratic" are all spelt correctly.

• Option 4 is correctly spelt throughout — "trinkets" and "gruesomely" are both spelt correctly.

NOTE

• Many English words ending in the sound "-ance/-ence" are commonly confused; remember: perseverance, appearance, attendance, relevance (with "-ance") versus existence, confidence, occurrence, reference (with "-ence") — these often need to be memorised individually as there is no single fixed rule.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world's children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. done to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes **"the harm ___ children", referring to harm that has been inflicted upon/caused to children. The correct collocation here is "harm done to (someone)", meaning damage or injury caused to that person/group.
◦ Example:** The harm done to the environment by plastic waste is irreversible.

• Grammatically, "done" is the past participle of "do", used here as a past participle modifying "harm" (i.e., "the harm [that is/has been] done to children"), fitting the passive, reduced-relative-clause structure of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "did to" is grammatically incorrect here, as "did" is a simple past finite verb and cannot follow the noun "harm" without a subject and auxiliary in this reduced clause structure.

• Option 3: "does to" is a present tense finite verb form and is grammatically unsuitable in this reduced participial construction after "harm".

• Option 4: "seems to" does not fit logically or grammatically, since "seems" is a linking verb that cannot combine with "harm" and "children" in this way to convey the intended meaning of harm being inflicted.

NOTE

• The collocation "harm done to" is a common fixed expression in formal/journalistic English; similar fixed phrases include "damage caused to", "injury inflicted on", and "loss suffered by".

As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. routine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence refers to **"setbacks to progress on ___ vaccinations", in the context of the pandemic disrupting normal, standard childhood immunization programmes. The word "routine" means regular, standard, and performed as a matter of course, which fits the context of ongoing, scheduled vaccination programmes that were disrupted by COVID-19.
◦ Example:** Routine childhood vaccinations against measles and polio were delayed during the pandemic.

• The passage as a whole discusses disruptions to normal/established systems (education, vaccination) caused by the pandemic, and "routine vaccinations" fits this theme of standard, ongoing healthcare services being set back.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "different" does not logically fit, as the sentence is not contrasting types of vaccinations but referring to standard, ongoing vaccination programmes.

• Option 2: "irregular" contradicts the intended meaning — the passage refers to setbacks in regular/standard vaccination programmes, not irregular ones.

• Option 4: "similar" does not fit the context, as there is no other set of vaccinations mentioned earlier in the sentence for "similar" to draw a comparison with.

NOTE

• In passages discussing healthcare/pandemic disruption, common collocations include: "routine check-ups", "routine immunization", and "routine screening" — all referring to regularly scheduled healthcare services.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world's children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has emerged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence **"That harm ___ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis" describes a past action (the harm coming into being) that has a direct and continuing relevance/connection to the present situation being described (2022, "increasingly evident"). This calls for the Present Perfect Tense**.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense: Formed with has/have + V3 (past participle), used for a past action whose effect/result continues to be relevant in the present. Since the subject "harm" is singular/uncountable, the auxiliary "has" is used.
◦ Structure: Subject (singular) + has + V3.

• Applying the rule: "harm has emerged" correctly conveys that this harm came about over recent time and continues to be evident now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "had emerged" is the Past Perfect Tense, used for an action completed before another past action; there is no such earlier past reference point in this sentence to justify the past perfect.

• Option 3: "have emerged" is grammatically incorrect here because the subject "harm" is singular/uncountable and requires the singular auxiliary "has", not "have".

• Option 4: "was emerged" is grammatically incorrect because "emerge" is an intransitive verb and cannot be used in the passive voice ("was + V3") — intransitive verbs do not take a passive form.

NOTE

• Intransitive verbs like emerge, occur, happen, arise, appear are never used in the passive voice, since they do not take a direct object.

• The Present Perfect Tense is commonly used in passages/reports to connect a past development to present relevance — a frequently tested concept in SSC exams.

2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world's children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. access to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"Lopsided ___ vaccines aside...", meaning that apart from the unequal/unbalanced availability of vaccines to different groups of people, other forms of harm are also being discussed. The correct word is "access", meaning the opportunity or right to obtain or make use of something, which correctly pairs with the preposition "to" to form the standard collocation "access to (something)".
◦ Example:** Access to clean drinking water remains unequal across regions.

• Rule — Collocation: The noun "access" is conventionally followed by the preposition "to" when specifying what is being accessed, e.g., "access to education", "access to healthcare", "access to vaccines".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "keeps to" does not make sense grammatically or contextually here, as "keeps" is a finite verb form that cannot follow the adjective "Lopsided" in this noun-phrase structure ("Lopsided ___ vaccines").

• Option 3: "seems to" is grammatically unsuitable in this position, as a noun is required after the adjective "Lopsided" (as in "Lopsided access"), not a linking-verb phrase.

• Option 4: "assess to" is grammatically incorrect, as "assess" is a verb that does not take the preposition "to" in standard usage (one assesses something, not "assesses to" something), and it does not fit the required noun-phrase structure.

NOTE

• Common noun + preposition collocations frequently tested in SSC: "access to", "solution to", "reaction to", "exposure to".

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

2022 sees us entering a third year of the pandemic, and the harm 1________ children is increasingly evident: A record rise in child poverty. Setbacks to progress on 2________ vaccinations. Disruption to education for entire generation. That harm 3________ as an unintended side effect of the world's efforts to manage the crisis.  COVID has been a uniquely dis-equalizing crisis. Lopsided 4________ vaccines aside, learning losses have been greatest among poorest children, and job losses have been disproportionately borne by women and youth.  What next for the world's children in the year ahead? As in the past two years, prospects for children will continue to hinge 5________ on the pandemic and how it is managed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. foremost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence states that **"prospects for children will continue to hinge ___ on the pandemic and how it is managed." The word "foremost" functions here as an adverb meaning "most importantly; above all else", and the phrase "hinge foremost on" conveys that the pandemic remains the single most important/primary factor determining children's future prospects.
◦ Example:** The success of the project will hinge foremost on adequate funding.

• Rule: "Hinge on/upon" is a fixed phrasal expression meaning "to depend entirely on something." Adding an intensifying adverb like "foremost" (similar to "chiefly" or "primarily") before "on" emphasises that this is the single most decisive factor among several.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "almost" does not fit logically, as "hinge almost on" would suggest an incomplete or partial dependence, which contradicts the passage's tone of the pandemic being the decisive/primary factor.

• Option 2: "minor" contradicts the intended meaning entirely, as it would suggest the pandemic is an insignificant factor, whereas the passage emphasises it as the key determinant of children's prospects.

• Option 4: "most" is grammatically awkward in this position ("hinge most on") and does not form as natural or idiomatic a collocation as "hinge foremost on" in this context.

NOTE

• The phrase "first and foremost" is a common idiomatic expression meaning "most importantly, before anything else" — frequently tested in SSC vocabulary and cloze-passage questions.

• Other verbs that pair with "on/upon" to mean "depend on": "depend on", "rely on", "rest on", "turn on".
